newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls Dec CPI data "good news".
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls Dec CPI data "good news".

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday that the December consumer price index was good news and offered proof that his economic strategy was working.

"This is good news for the American people and more evidence that our economic strategy is working," Clinton said in a statement after the release of the CPI data, which showed a 0.3 percent rise last month. Excluding food and energy, the index rose by 0.1 percent.
"The report cofirms that the combined rate of unemployment and inflation -- the so-called Misery Index -- was lower in 1996 than in any year since 1968," Clinton said.

The statement added that in the past three years the United States has enjoyed stronger real average hourly wage growth than in any three-year period in nearly two decades, exceeded only by the 1976-1978 period.

"We will continue our efforts to reduce the deficit to zero, expand trade and increase educational opportunities," Clinton added. "Now is the time to work together in a bipartisan fashion and build on our success."
